description: BID bid_id JSON PATH IS PARTIALLY WRONG / UNVERIFIED. Real `provider-services query market bid list -o json` returns bids as `{"bids":[{"bid":{"bid_id":{"owner":..,"dseq":..,"gseq":N,"oseq":N,"provider":..},"state":"open","price":{..}}, "escrow_account":{..}}]}`. The script reads `.bids[0].bid.bid_id` (line 78) then `.gseq/.oseq/.provider` (line 83) — gseq/oseq/provider DO live in bid_id, so that part is plausible. HOWEVER (a) the script does NOT filter `--state open`, so a closed/lost bid could be picked as `[0]`; (b) it blindly takes `[0]` instead of the lowest-price open bid; (c) gseq/oseq in real JSON may be integers, and they are interpolated unquoted into the lease command which is fine, but the script never validates they are non-empty/non-null before building the lease tx. The fake at test-deploy-akash.sh:36 returns an IDEALIZED shape `{"bids":[{"bid":{"bid_id":{"gseq":1,"oseq":1,"provider":"akash1prov"}}}]}` that omits owner/dseq/state/price, so the oracle cannot catch a state-filter or price-selection bug and cannot prove the real nested path beyond what the builder assumed.

evidence.snippet: BID="$(... | jq -c '.bids[0].bid.bid_id // empty')" ... GSEQ="$(jq -r '.gseq' <<<"$BID")"; OSEQ=...; PROVIDER=...

correctFix: Add `--state open` to the bid query; select the cheapest open bid, e.g. `jq -c '[.bids[]|select(.bid.state=="open")]|sort_by(.bid.price.amount|tonumber)|.[0].bid.bid_id // empty'`. Guard each of GSEQ/OSEQ/PROVIDER for empty/null before the lease tx and fail-closed otherwise. Make the fake emit the full real bid shape (owner,dseq,gseq,oseq,provider,state,price + escrow_account) so the oracle exercises the real path.
